verdict: HCA's revenue grew 3.6% on more patients, but a shift toward uninsured patients cost about $400 million and net income fell 3.9%.

segments.name: Hospitals & care sites
segments.note: 189 hospitals and about 2,600 ambulatory care sites in 19 states and the U.K. HCA reports as a single segment.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of hospitals, equipment and systems over their useful lives (a non-cash charge).

otherDetail: Interest expense of $607 million, partly offset by $20 million of equity earnings from affiliates and a $13 million gain on sales of facilities — a net $574 million cost.
follow100Note: Direct costs here are the cost of caring for patients: salaries and benefits $8,581M, supplies $2,822M and other operating expenses $4,548M. Kept as profit is total net income of $1,849M; $1,579M is attributable to HCA shareholders and $270M to noncontrolling interests.

takeaways.title: More patients came in
takeaways.text: Same-facility equivalent admissions rose 3.0% and emergency room visits rose 5.1%, driving revenue up 3.6% to $19.8 billion.

takeaways.title: Uninsured mix hurt profit
takeaways.text: More patients arrived without insurance as exchange coverage lapsed — HCA estimates a roughly $400 million pre-tax hit in the quarter, and net income attributable fell 3.9% to $1.58 billion.

takeaways.title: EPS still rose, on buybacks
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS rose 4.5% to $7.27 even as profit fell, because HCA repurchased 7.2 million shares for $3.0 billion in the quarter, shrinking the share count.

oneTimers: Results include a $13 million gain on sales of facilities ($0.05 per share), versus a $2 million loss a year ago.
